# Motorsport playbook

Use these as research dimensions and hypotheses, not universal operator facts. Assume US focus only provisionally if region is unspecified. Racing schools, track rentals, experience rides, HPDE coaching and competition arrive-and-drive are distinct offers.

## Racing schools

Explore beginner confidence, progression from simulation/HPDE, license eligibility, coaching quality and useful driving time. Compare objective, prerequisite, car, venue, actual sessions/seat time, instructor ratio, feedback/telemetry, equipment, schedule and total cost. Time at the venue is not seat time; completing a course or attending an accredited school does not guarantee a competition license.

Let undecided buyers compare relevant programs by goal, with a fast path for buyers who know their program. Track pages need verified reasons to drive there, logistics/facilities, relevant onboard footage with rights/embedding checked and available programs. Avoid interchangeable descriptions.

## Track-car rental

Determine event format, circuit/date, experience, eligible car, shared/exclusive use, sessions/mileage, instruction and support. Show whether entry, fuel, consumables, transport, crew, equipment and taxes are included. Road-rental eligibility does not establish track eligibility.

Availability can depend jointly on car, instructor, transport, event slot and maintenance status. Test conflicts. Verify policies for cancellation, weather, mechanical failure, replacement cars, extra drivers and damage handling.

## Upsells and proof

Consider coaching, video/data review, extra sessions, additional drivers and eligible protection products only when actually offered. Distinguish insurance, damage-liability reduction, refundable deposit and trip cancellation. Preserve provider terms, exclusions, excess/deductible and eligibility; never invent coverage. Show optional choices and total price before purchase.

Use approved credentials, genuine testimony, relevant footage and specific program facts. Do not fabricate reviews, scarcity, lap-time guarantees, seat time or safety claims. Keep unknowns explicit; resolve conflicting public claims with current owner evidence.

## Examples checked 2026-09-13

- https://www.skipbarber.com/faq illustrates program-specific prerequisites and dates/cars varying by venue. Recheck before using operator facts.
- https://rsrnurburg.com/track-insurance-and-accidents/ illustrates differing responsibilities for deposits, damage excess and separately arranged insurance. This European operator is not a US policy template.

## PTC context

PTC is a potential design partner, not a signed client or measured win. User preferences: sell program choice visibly, explain track differentiation, include relevant onboards and supported upsells. The PTC concept is intended to replace booking; TrackRabbit may guide required information but must not be integrated directly. Keep that constraint PTC-specific; establish other clients’ integration choices separately.
